around.headline: Bengaluru techie drowns in quarry during Instagram-group trek; body found after 2-day search
around.summary: The Times of India reports the techie drowned in a quarry on a trek organised through an Instagram group, and the body was found after a two-day search. Quarry water is deep and unpredictable, so skip swimming at such spots, especially with groups you don't know.

around.headline: Fake medicine racket: Kingpin's Turkiye link exposed
around.summary: The Times of India reports new details of a fake medicine racket, with the kingpin's Turkiye link exposed. Buy medicines from licensed chemists and check batch number and packaging before use.

around.headline: Race Course Road: 60-day traffic curbs from Oct 5
around.summary: Deccan Herald and the Times of India report that part of Race Course Road is shut from today with diversions for 60 days. Plan alternate routes before leaving, especially with rain expected.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Times of India

around.headline: Pink Line underground section: systems work nearly complete, trial run before 2026 ends
around.summary: Deccan Herald reports systems work on the Pink Line underground section is nearly complete, with a trial run planned before the end of 2026. This is a trial run, not passenger service yet.

around.headline: Bengaluru traffic violations hit five-year high in 8 months
around.summary: Deccan Herald reports traffic violations in the city are at a five-year high for the first eight months of the year. Keep your helmet and documents in order, since enforcement is likely to stay tight.

around.headline: Citizens give private land for road widening; Nallurhalli traffic to ease
around.summary: The Times of India reports residents have handed over private land to widen roads, which should ease Nallurhalli traffic. Good news for commuters on that stretch once work is done.

around.headline: Supreme Court to hear petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over SIR decisions
around.summary: Live Law reports the Supreme Court will hear petitions over the Election Commission's SIR decisions, while protests continue in Delhi. The case concerns the process of updating voter rolls, so check that your name is on the electoral roll.

street_smart.title: You're on a weekend trek organised through an Instagram group and the group stops at a scenic quarry lake. Everyone is jumping in; you don't know the depth and there's no lifeguard. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Times of India, Oct 5: Bengaluru techie drowns in quarry during Instagram-group trek; body found after 2-day search.
street_smart.situation: The group leader, someone you met online yesterday, says the water is 'fine' and the others are already swimming. The water is murky and there is no rope, tube or rescue help nearby.

choices.text: Stay out of the water, enjoy the view from the bank, and suggest the group does the same.
choices.feedback: Quarry pits have sheer, uneven walls, sudden depth, cold layers and hidden debris, and murky water hides all of it. Even good swimmers get into trouble because there is no shallow edge to stand on or climb out from.

choices.text: Jump in with the group since everyone else is doing it.
choices.feedback: Group pressure makes a spot look safe because others are in it. Drowning is quiet, and nobody beside you may notice, and an online group leader has no verified training or rescue gear.

choices.text: Wade in only up to your waist and stay near the edge.
choices.feedback: Quarry edges can drop away suddenly and slopes are slippery. A slip near the edge can put you into deep water in a step.

choices.text: Swim, but ask someone to film you so there is a record if anything happens.
choices.feedback: A camera is not a rescuer. Without a trained person, a float and a plan, filming only records a problem.

takeaways: Avoid swimming in quarries, lakes and ponds with no lifeguard, however calm they look.
Before joining a group trek, check who runs it, ask about safety gear and a first-aid person, and share your location with family.
In an emergency call 112 (or 108 for an ambulance); reach with a rope or pole, don't jump in after the person.

quiz.question: For how many days are traffic curbs on part of Race Course Road in force from Oct 5?
quiz.why: Diversions run for 60 days. Race Course Road runs beside the Bangalore Turf Club grounds in the central city.

quiz.question: Which Bengaluru metro line's underground section is nearing a trial run before 2026 ends?
quiz.why: Deccan Herald reports systems work on the Pink Line underground section is nearly complete. It is the line with underground stretches in the central city.

quiz.question: The Supreme Court is hearing petitions against which Election Commission decisions, as reported today?
quiz.why: Petitions challenge the CEC's SIR decisions. The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body created under Article 324.

quiz.question: Which of these is the largest planet in our Solar System?
quiz.why: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

quiz.question: What does the 'G' in GST stand for?
quiz.why: GST is Goods and Services Tax, introduced in India on 1 July 2017 and replacing many indirect taxes such as VAT and service tax.
